newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN CALL MONEY FIRMS ON TALK OF BUBA REPO MOVE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN CALL MONEY FIRMS ON TALK OF BUBA REPO MOVE.

text.p: German call money rates firmed on Thursday amid speculation the Bundesbank may signal higher interest rates at next week's auction for securities repurchase agreements, or repos, money dealers said.
The interest rate on overnight money rose as high as 3.15 percent, and traded in a range of 3.10 to 3.15 percent, up from 3.00 to 3.10 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said the rise was explained by a drop in market liquidity as banks held on to funds in the belief that the central bank may make it more expensive to obtain money next week.
"The rate rise is linked to speculation about next week's auction," one money dealer said.
Speculation has mounted that the Bundesbank may raise interest rates to stem the mark's slide against the dollar.

Frankfurt money dealers said the Bundesbank may return to variable-rate tender for repo funds, a system in which the repo rate -- the Bundesbank's main money market rate -- is determined by the rate at which the banks bid for funds.
The repo rate has been fixed by the Bundesbank at 3.00 percent since August 1996.
Dealers said the variable-rate repo may be offered in conjunction with a fixed-rate repo to prevent money market rates from rising too high.
"There's a danger that the market might overreact if the Bundesbank were just to set a variable-rate repo. It would immediately affect longer-term money rates," one dealer said.

A two-week fixed-rate repo tender, set in conjunction with a four-week variable-rate tender, would give markets a signal where the Bundesbank wants to see the repo rate and would prevent a surge in the rate, dealers said.
"With just a variable-rate repo, the Bundesbank would be sounding the attack. But whatever change the Bundesbank makes to the repo, the market will interpret it that the rate cycle has turned."
One dealer said the Bundesbank may keep its fixed repo at 3.00 percent and set a variable repo at the same time.
Dealers said they did not expect call money rates to rise much further from current levels in the coming days.
Wednesday's surprisingly large net addition of 2.6 billion marks at the Bundesbank's weekly repo tender had dampened expectations of a switch to a higher repo rate next week.
A smaller addition would have been interpreted as a means to keep the market short of liquidity and prepare the ground for higher rates.

But dealers on Thursday said the addition appeared to have purely been dictated by the Bundesbank's perception of how much money the market needed after bank deposits at the Bundesbank -- a measure of market liquidity -- fell sharply this week.
On Wednesday, commercial banks' deposits at the Bundesbank rose to 41.2 billion marks from 39.0 billion. The average for the month rose to 40.8 billion marks from 40.7 billion marks.
Borrowings from the Bundesbank's Lombard facility rose to about 600 million marks from 200 million.
